meta.description: Each accommodation is stored once in library; byCode lists which ones are suggested for each ICD-10-CM code.

clear-direct-instructions.name: Clear & Direct Instructions
clear-direct-instructions.reason: processes information most effectively when instructions are explicit, concrete, and provided in writing
clear-direct-instructions.recommendation: receive written instructions and rubrics for all major assignments and have the opportunity to ask clarifying questions

sensory-breaks.name: Sensory Breaks
sensory-breaks.reason: can experience sensory overstimulation in a typical classroom environment
sensory-breaks.recommendation: be permitted to use noise-cancelling headphones or step out for brief sensory breaks to prevent overwhelm

extended-time.name: Extended Time
extended-time.reason: can have trouble with sustained focus and time management, which can impact their ability to complete tasks within standard time limits
extended-time.recommendation: receive 1.5x the standard time for all exams and have the ability to request a 48-hour extension on major assignments when communicated in advance

quiet-testing-environment.name: Quiet Testing Environment
quiet-testing-environment.reason: can be easily distracted by auditory or visual stimuli in a standard classroom setting
quiet-testing-environment.recommendation: be provided a separate, quiet room for all major exams to minimize distractions

movement-breaks.name: Movement Breaks
movement-breaks.reason: may experience hyperactivity and have difficulty remaining seated for long periods
movement-breaks.recommendation: be allowed to take short, discreet movement breaks, such as standing in the back of the room or walking out for a minute.

use-of-fidget-tools.name: Use of Fidget Tools
use-of-fidget-tools.reason: can improve focus and manage hyperactivity through small, non-disruptive motor movements
use-of-fidget-tools.recommendation: be permitted to use quiet fidget tools in the classroom to aid concentration.

use-of-assistive-technology.name: Use of Assistive Technology
use-of-assistive-technology.reason: has specific deficits in reading, writing, or math that can be supported by technology
use-of-assistive-technology.recommendation: be permitted to use text-to-speech, speech-to-text software, or calculators as appropriate for their specific learning disability.

alternative-formats-for-materials.name: Alternative Formats for Materials
alternative-formats-for-materials.reason: may struggle with standard print materials
alternative-formats-for-materials.recommendation: be provided with course materials in an alternative format, such as audiobooks, large print, or digital text that can be used with assistive technology.

note-taking-assistance.name: Note-Taking Assistance
note-taking-assistance.reason: may have difficulty with concentration and auditory processing, making it challenging to simultaneously listen, comprehend, and take comprehensive notes
note-taking-assistance.recommendation: be provided with a peer note-taker or be permitted to audio-record lectures to ensure they can review the material accurately.

flexible-attendance.name: Flexible Attendance
flexible-attendance.reason: may experience fluctuations in symptoms that can impact their ability to attend class consistently
flexible-attendance.recommendation: have an agreed-upon number of excused absences without penalty and be able to obtain materials for any missed classes.

reduced-distraction-environment-for-exam.name: Reduced Distraction Environment for Exams
reduced-distraction-environment-for-exam.reason: is susceptible to sensory overstimulation and distracting internal thoughts, which can interfere with performance in a standard testing environment
reduced-distraction-environment-for-exam.recommendation: take all exams in a separate, quiet room to minimize distractions.

deadline-and-exam-flexibility.name: Deadline and Exam Flexibility
deadline-and-exam-flexibility.reason: experiences cyclical mood and thought disruptions that can unpredictably affect their ability to complete work and prepare for exams
deadline-and-exam-flexibility.recommendation: have the ability to request extensions on assignments and, in coordination with the professor, reschedule an exam if symptoms are acute.

structured-feedback.name: Structured Feedback
structured-feedback.reason: benefits from clear, concrete, and structured feedback to aid with focus and reduce potential for misinterpretation during periods of cognitive stress
structured-feedback.recommendation: receive assignment feedback in writing and have the opportunity to ask clarifying questions with the instructor or a TA.

attendance-and-deadline-flexibility.name: Attendance and Deadline Flexibility
attendance-and-deadline-flexibility.reason: experiences significant variations in energy, concentration, and motivation due to mood episodes (manic and depressive)
attendance-and-deadline-flexibility.recommendation: be granted flexibility on attendance and assignment deadlines, with a clear communication plan established with the professor.

breaks-during-class-and-exams.name: Breaks During Class and Exams
breaks-during-class-and-exams.reason: may experience racing thoughts or psychomotor agitation during manic phases, or fatigue and cognitive slowing during depressive phases
breaks-during-class-and-exams.recommendation: be permitted to take short, unobtrusive breaks during long classes or exams as needed to manage symptoms.

reduced-course-load.name: Reduced Course Load
reduced-course-load.reason: may find a full course load overwhelming while managing symptoms, which can exacerbate mood episodes
reduced-course-load.recommendation: be permitted to take a reduced course load without affecting their status as a student.

flexible-deadlines.name: Flexible Deadlines
flexible-deadlines.reason: may face challenges with motivation, energy levels, and concentration, making it difficult to complete assignments on a fixed schedule
flexible-deadlines.recommendation: be able to negotiate deadline extensions with professors, especially for larger projects, when symptoms are present.

support-with-participation.name: Support with Participation
support-with-participation.reason: may find it difficult to engage in classroom discussions due to low energy or feelings of worthlessness
support-with-participation.recommendation: be allowed to participate in alternative ways, such as through online discussion boards or one-on-one meetings with the instructor.

alternative-to-in-class-presentations.name: Alternative to In-Class Presentations
alternative-to-in-class-presentations.reason: experiences intense fear and anxiety related to public speaking or being in front of a large group
alternative-to-in-class-presentations.recommendation: be provided with an alternative to oral presentations, such as a written paper, a pre-recorded presentation, or a one-on-one presentation with the instructor.

advance-notice-for-group-work.name: Advance notice for group work
advance-notice-for-group-work.reason: may require mental preparation for group interactions
advance-notice-for-group-work.recommendation: be given advance notice for group projects to mentally prepare and manage anxiety.

extended-time-on-exams.name: Extended Time on Exams
extended-time-on-exams.reason: may experience cognitive difficulties, such as racing thoughts or trouble concentrating, due to anxiety
extended-time-on-exams.recommendation: receive 1.5x the standard time on all exams and timed assignments.

ability-to-take-breaks.name: Ability to Take Breaks
ability-to-take-breaks.reason: may experience sudden, intense episodes of panic
ability-to-take-breaks.recommendation: be permitted to leave the classroom without penalty if they experience a panic attack.

preferential-seating.name: Preferential Seating
preferential-seating.reason: may experience intense anxiety or panic in crowded spaces or situations where they feel 'trapped'
preferential-seating.recommendation: be allowed to sit near an exit to ease feelings of confinement and allow for a quick departure if symptoms escalate.

flexible-deadlines-2.name: Flexible Deadlines
flexible-deadlines-2.reason: experiences symptoms of anxiety that can be exacerbated by rigid deadlines, impacting their ability to produce work that reflects their knowledge
flexible-deadlines-2.recommendation: be permitted to request a 2-3 day extension on assignments when needed, in communication with the professor

ability-to-take-breaks-2.name: Ability to Take Breaks
ability-to-take-breaks-2.reason: may experience episodes of heightened anxiety or panic during long lectures or exams
ability-to-take-breaks-2.recommendation: be allowed to step out of the classroom or testing environment for short breaks without penalty, as needed to manage symptoms

flexibility-on-timed-assignments.name: Flexibility on Timed Assignments
flexibility-on-timed-assignments.reason: may engage in compulsive behaviors or require extra time for re-checking work due to obsessional thoughts, which can be debilitating under timed pressure
flexibility-on-timed-assignments.recommendation: be granted extended time (1.5x or 2x) on all timed exams and in-class assignments

preferential-seating-2.name: Preferential Seating
preferential-seating-2.reason: may experience hypervigilance and can be easily startled or triggered by their surroundings
preferential-seating-2.recommendation: be permitted to choose seating near an exit or at the back of the room to minimize feelings of being trapped or surrounded

advance-notice-of-content.name: Advance Notice of Content
advance-notice-of-content.reason: can be activated by specific topics or content that may be triggering
advance-notice-of-content.recommendation: receive advance notice or a content warning for potentially graphic or traumatic material discussed in lectures or required readings

flexible-deadlines-3.name: Flexible Deadlines
flexible-deadlines-3.reason: is experiencing significant distress while adjusting to a new stressor, which can temporarily impact their academic functioning
flexible-deadlines-3.recommendation: be granted short-term flexibility with deadlines as they navigate their situation.

memory-aids.name: Memory Aids
memory-aids.reason: may experience memory gaps or difficulty recalling information due to dissociative symptoms
memory-aids.recommendation: be permitted to use an instructor-approved note sheet or memory aid during exams.

rest-breaks.name: Rest Breaks
rest-breaks.reason: may experience dissociative episodes that require a moment to reorient and ground themselves
rest-breaks.recommendation: be allowed to take short breaks during exams and classes in a pre-arranged quiet space.

flexible-attendance-2.name: Flexible Attendance
flexible-attendance-2.reason: may have frequent medical appointments or periods of intense health-related anxiety that affect their ability to attend class
flexible-attendance-2.recommendation: have flexibility with attendance, with a clear plan for making up missed work.

medical-absence-flexibility.name: Medical Absence Flexibility
medical-absence-flexibility.reason: requires ongoing medical and therapeutic appointments that may conflict with class schedules
medical-absence-flexibility.recommendation: have excused absences for treatment-related appointments without penalty.

alternative-to-food-related-assignments.name: Alternative to Food-Related Assignments
alternative-to-food-related-assignments.reason: may find assignments involving nutrition, meal planning, or food-centric cultural discussions to be triggering
alternative-to-food-related-assignments.recommendation: be offered alternative assignments or topics in courses like health or nutrition.

choice-in-assignments.name: Choice in Assignments
choice-in-assignments.reason: may exhibit oppositional behavior when feeling a lack of control
choice-in-assignments.recommendation: be provided with choices in assignment topics or formats, where possible, to increase buy-in and cooperation.

non-confrontational-redirection.name: Non-Confrontational Redirection
non-confrontational-redirection.reason: can escalate in response to direct confrontation
non-confrontational-redirection.recommendation: be redirected using non-confrontational language and offered a chance to cool down in a designated space if behavior becomes disruptive.

cooling-off-period.name: Cooling-Off Period
cooling-off-period.reason: may experience sudden outbursts of anger or aggression
cooling-off-period.recommendation: be allowed to leave the classroom for a pre-arranged 'cooling-off' space when they feel their anger escalating, without penalty.

behavioral-contracts.name: Behavioral Contracts
behavioral-contracts.reason: benefits from clear, predictable rules and consequences to help manage behavior
behavioral-contracts.recommendation: establish a behavioral contract with clear expectations for classroom conduct and assignment completion, co-created with the student and instructor.

positive-reinforcement.name: Positive Reinforcement
positive-reinforcement.reason: responds well to positive reinforcement for meeting behavioral and academic goals
positive-reinforcement.recommendation: implement a system that acknowledges and rewards progress towards positive classroom engagement.

clear-and-direct-communication.name: Clear and Direct Communication
clear-and-direct-communication.reason: may have difficulties with interpersonal relationships and interpreting social cues
clear-and-direct-communication.recommendation: benefit from clear, explicit, and written communication regarding expectations and feedback to avoid misunderstandings.

emotionally-regulated-feedback.name: Emotionally Regulated Feedback
emotionally-regulated-feedback.reason: may experience intense emotional reactions to perceived criticism
emotionally-regulated-feedback.recommendation: receive feedback in a structured, non-evaluative, and private manner to help manage emotional responses.
